checks.what: Sweden gains from Denmark-Norway, Jan 1670, the Danish-Norwegian cells inside present Sweden. Page: Brömsebro 1645 ceded 'Jemtland, Herjedalen and Idre & Serna'; Roskilde (26 February 1658) ceded 'Båhuslen' and the Scanian lands; Copenhagen 1660 gave back only 'Trøndelag and Bornholm'. The spec 'Sweden minus (Norway ∪ Denmark)' resolves to the same 2,440 cells as Sweden: the minus is a no-op, and the text wrongly said it cut the border cells. A gain takes only the cells the counterpart holds. With the other windows' patches the trial moves 3 cells, not about 50: Jämtland at 63.18N 12.17E and 64.54N 13.83E, Idre at 61.69N 12.22E. The rest were already Swedish. Works only together with keyframe_overrides/5.

checks.what: Awlad Muhammad gain of the Fezzan in 1679 from the Ottoman empire, reversing the dossier's ledger/3 (loss 1679). Fezzan page: 'It was occupied fully from times to time like in 1679-1682, 1690, 1716, 1718 and 1811/1812'. Awlad Muhammad page: in 1682 an Ottoman army under Murad al-Malti killed the sultan, and 'His son, Sultan Muhammad al-Nasir, agreed to pay tribute', so the dynasty went on. The region is the dossier's own Fezzan spec (2,033 cells). Trial: 2,033 cells go from Ottoman direct to Awlad land under Ottoman occupation in 1679.

Occupation_start 1679 of the Fezzan by the Ottoman empire; same page sentence ('occupied fully ... 1679-1682'). The counterpart follows the dossier's ledger/3. Trial: the packet shows 'occupation of awlad-muhammad-dynasty's land by ottoman-empire, 2033 cells, since 1679, open at the end'.

Occupation_end 1682, the end of the page's span '1679-1682'. The dossier's ledger/4 (1682 gain) then moves nothing. It is dated outside the window, applied with a note and flagged by the window agent.

qing-dynasty_1673 limited to 1673-1673. Without from/to it took Cliopatria's span 1673-1676, and its wide shape (Qing minus Yunnan and Guizhou) entered the union at the 1674 snap. That handed Hunan, Sichuan and Guangxi back to the Qing in 1674-1675. Page: 'In December 1673, Wu Sangui ended his connection to the Qing dynasty'; 'Wu's forces captured Hunan and Sichuan provinces'; Sun Yanling 'rose in revolt in Guangxi'; 'In 1680, the provinces of Hunan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and Sichuan were recovered by the Qing'. Trial: 2,755 cells go from Qing to Wu in 1674-1675. The 1676 Wu snap of 2,841 cells is gone. 1673 is unchanged.

wu-sangui-s-zhou_1676 without Fujian. The Revolt page dates no surrender: 'after 1676, the tide turned in favor of the Qing forces ... Geng Jingzhong and Shang Zhixin surrendered in turn'. The Geng Jingzhong page, opened in this review, does: 'in 1674 Geng Jingzhong rebelled against Qing rule'; he 'surrendered in 1676 and pledged his support to putting down the other revolting feudatories'. That matches the dossier's ledger/5. Guangdong in 1676 stays supported: 'In 1676, Shang Zhixin joined the rebellion, consolidating Guangdong under his rule'. Region: the six provinces (Sichuan with Chongqing), as the dossier.
checks.fix: Source changed to the Geng Jingzhong page, which carries the dated sentence; the quote added to why.

checks.what: qing-dynasty_1676 with Fujian back after Geng's 1676 surrender (Geng Jingzhong page, as above). Those are Xiamen, Quanzhou and Zhangzhou, which kingdom-of-tungning_1674 holds to 1676. Kingdom of Tungning page: 'Zheng captured Quanzhou and Zhangzhou in 1674'; Quanzhou 'was lost to the Qing on 12 March 1677'. checks.fix: Added to the minus: Xiamen 40 km, Quanzhou 50 km, Zhangzhou 50 km (the circles of kingdom-of-tungning_1674); source set to the Geng Jingzhong page; Tungning page quoted in why.

checks.what: qing-dynasty_1677 = Cliopatria Qing 1677 ∪ (Southern Ming 1677 row minus Wu's core and Taiwan). Without the patch, the 1677 snap left 1,810 Qing cells nobody's to 1679: Guangdong 691, Fujian 488, Hubei 230, Shaanxi 132, Gansu 112, Jiangxi 102, Zhejiang 23, other 32. These are the provinces the ledger had already returned. Support: 'after 1676, the tide turned'; Wang Fuchen 'surrendered after a three-year-long stalemate'. The Shang Zhixin page has him defect back 'after Shang Kexi's death in late 1676'. Only Hunan, Guizhou, Guangxi and Sichuan are recovered in 1680. Revolt page: 'Zheng Jing's forces were defeated near Xiamen in 1680'. Tungning page: Haicheng retaken 'in August' 1677, and the mainland war closed 'On 10 April' 1680. Corrected trial: Tungning holds 161 cells in 1677-1679 (window's version 132/102, no patch 136); the Qing still gets the 1,810 cells. Render of 1678 checked.
checks.fix: Correction wrapped as minus [the window's union, union(Xiamen 40 km, Zhangzhou 50 km, Chaozhou 50 km)] (the circles of kingdom-of-tungning_1677); why extended.

checks.what: qing-dynasty_1678 (1678-1679) has the same construction plus Hunan, and the same Tungning defect. Both shapes are alive in 1678, so both needed the cut. Hunan stays mostly Wu's by the size rule; the Qing hold the Hengzhou, Changde and Yuezhou circles (Wu ledger/11). The 1678 render matches this.

denmark-norway_1670 (1670-1708) without present Sweden. Page as events/0. The inner spec 'Sweden minus (Norway ∪ Denmark)' was a no-op written as if it cut border cells. The new 23-cell Denmark-Norway/Holstein conflict in 1670 also appears in a trial without this patch, so it is not caused here.
checks.fix: Inner spec written as {country: Sweden} (same cells) with an accurate text; correction text shortened.

checks.what: new-france_1670 plus Acadia: the Nova Scotia and New Brunswick cells of Cliopatria's 1673 shape. This is the same spec as the dossier's ledger/13 (1670 gain from the English), so the 1670 snap no longer throws them away. Acadia page: England controlled the area 'again from 1654 until 1670'; capital 'Castine, Maine (1670–1674)'. Trial: 53 cells go from nobody to New France (French colony tint) in 1670-1672. The 1670 snap's removals fall from 69 to 16; those 16 were already there without the patch.

spanish-empire_1677 cut to 1677-1679, keeping New Mexico. Page: Pueblo Revolt 'August 10–21, 1680'; the Spaniards then retreated toward El Paso del Norte. In the 1670s there was drought and unrest ('came to a head in 1675'), not a withdrawal. In the current compile New Mexico is viceroyalty-of-new-spain's (p1600-p1609 events/0), whose ledger/3 loses it in 1680. The Spanish 1677 snap does not fire with or without this entry, so it moves no cell now; it is harmless and consistent with the page. Its correction text was a garbled merge that said 'New Mexico removed from 1680 ... the shape is otherwise unchanged'.
checks.fix: Correction text rewritten to describe the spec (Cliopatria 1677 with New Mexico, minus the Maguindanao and Buayan cores); why notes that it currently moves nothing.

Systemic, R2: qing-dynasty is listed as kingdom-of-tungning's successor, so it wins every conflict with Tungning from its own start year (1644), not from the 1683 takeover. Still 28 cells in 1674 (kingdom-of-tungning_1674 against the Qing) and 2 in 1677 go to the Qing. Any Qing keyframe covering Zheng's mainland holds takes them. Fix in the rules or in the dossier: R2 should act only from the successor's taking of the land.

Boundary: keyframe_overrides/3 (qing-dynasty_1677) keeps its Cliopatria span 1677-1682 and joins the union at the 1680 and 1682 snaps. It is narrower than p1680-p1689's qing-dynasty_1680 override and the dossier's _1682, so it has no effect there. Tungning's ledger/11 (April 1680) hands Xiamen, Haicheng and Chaozhou to the Qing.

Boundary: keyframe_overrides/5 (denmark-norway_1670) spans 1670-1708 but affects only the 1670 snap. events/3 closes the Fezzan occupation in 1682, so p1680-p1689 sees it open on 1 January 1680. keyframe_overrides/7 leaves no spanish-empire keyframe alive in 1680-1682, which is harmless: New Mexico is New Spain's and its ledger/3 removes it in 1680.
